_comment: Questions for the UFV Campus VLM evaluation. Two perception experiments (Exp1, Exp2). Production-aligned structured-output prompts live in prompts.json (Exp3). Each question declares which categories it applies to and the metric subset it contributes to.

experiment1.name: Perception (state and element classification)
experiment1.description: Evaluates the VLM's generic perception capability: identifying the main element shown in the image (multi-class) and classifying state or sub-type for each element (binary closed-class).

questions.question_text: What type of object is shown in this image? Reply with exactly one word from this list: stairs, elevator.
questions.note: Multi-class classification over the two architectural elements (stairs, elevator). Bathroom verification is moved to Phase B with a dedicated arrival-verification prompt.

questions.question_text: Looking at the staircase from the camera's point of view, are the stairs going up or down? Reply with exactly one word from this list: up, down.
Look at the elevator doors in this image. Are they open or closed? Reply with exactly one word from this list: open, closed.

experiment2.name: Location extraction
experiment2.description: Evaluates the VLM's ability to extract location information from directory signs and classroom door plates (free-form text extraction, scored by component accuracy and substring match).

questions.question_text: Look at this directory sign. The location indicator is shown in the top-right area of the sign. What location does it indicate? Reply with exactly one of these strings: G 0, G 1, G 2, or G Agora.
What room code is shown on this plate? Answer with only the room code.
questions.note: room_code_accuracy uses substring match with word-boundary against the expected code.

notes: Each question declares its applicable categories and (optionally) a sub-set filter via 'applies_only_when_field_equals'.
Ground-truth values per image live in ground_truth.json (referenced by 'ground_truth_file' in this metadata).
Production-aligned structured-output prompts (PDDL atoms, JSON objects) live in prompts.json and are evaluated by Exp3.
